text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Productivity and Standards Board arranges mentoring scheme for companies to help each other and to set industry benchmarks.
- David Chan, leader of Hongkong protest voyage to Diaoyu islands, jumps into sea and drowns.
- North Korea warns it would take strong counter-measures against South Korea for hunting down escaped crew of wrecked spy submarine.
- Wing Tai Holdings-led group clinches purchase of Cockpit Hotel and adjoining property for Singapore $380 million.
- Telecommunication Authority of Singapore says it will divest most, if not all, of its 40 percent stake in the Singapore ONE infrastructure consortium .
- Stock Exchange of Singapore warns it will come down hard on stock brokers who allow clients to roll over overdue purchases.
- Property magnate Ng Teng Fong and son Robert among 5,800 people seeking places in Hongkong's nominated 400-member panel that will elect chief executive under Chinese rule.
- Plastic and metal component maker NatSteel Broadway will raise US$22.46 million from initial public offering of 33.8 million shares which launches at 70 US cents each.
- Infrastructure contractor Ipco International with two other companies forms joint venture company to operate water and waste water projects and concessions in Brazil.
- Robinson & Company intends to expand all its retail chains despite company's forecast of flat profits and sluggish market conditions.
